svg.title: Anatomy of a window's spectrum: main lobe and side lobes
svg.desc: The spectrum a Hann window gives a single tone, in decibels, from 10 bins below to 10 bins above the tone, with the rectangular window's spectrum in grey for comparison. The Hann main lobe reaches its first nulls 2 bins either side of the tone; it is 1.44 bins wide at -3 dB and 2 bins wide at -6 dB. Half a bin from the centre it is 1.42 dB down, which is the scalloping loss. Its highest side lobe is -31.5 dB and the side lobes fall by about 18 dB per octave. The rectangular window's main lobe is narrower, with nulls at plus and minus 1 bin, but its highest side lobe is -13.3 dB and its side lobes fall by only 6 dB per octave.
svg.text: A window's spectrum: one main lobe, many side lobes
Level in dB for a single tone at bin 0, Hann window (blue) and no window (grey)
side lobes fall 18 dB per octave
